title: Fraction word problems (model method)
examples: How do I know when to use the model method?
Can you show me another example of remainder-of-remainder?
Is this always about finding a part of a whole?

explain.say: Today we learn to solve fraction word problems using a model.
First we look at fractions represented by bars for clear understanding.
For example if a bar is divided into four parts, one part is one fourth.
Next we learn about remainder-of-remainder problems in fractions.

items: Take away the second fraction from what remains

explain.say: For instance if you have one whole, and take away one third, then take away one sixth.
In real life you might share leftover pizza slices with friends.

faq.q: What is the model method really for?
faq.a: It helps you visualize how fractions relate to a whole amount. You can also use it to see how parts fit together.
asks: How do I picture the problem?

faq.a: You use it when you take away one part, and then take away another part from what is left. It is a two-step subtraction.
asks: Does the second subtraction use the remainder?
What is the difference from simple subtraction?

faq.q: Do I need to find a common denominator first?
faq.a: Yes, when adding or subtracting fractions, you must find a common denominator first. This keeps the parts the same size.
asks: Must I make the denominators match?
Can I add fractions with different bottoms?
What if the denominators are prime numbers?

faq.q: Is this only for improper fractions?
faq.a: No, you can use this method for proper fractions too. The whole bar can represent one whole unit.
asks: Does this work for fractions less than one?

faq.q: What if the problem gives two different wholes?
faq.a: If the problem mentions two separate wholes, you might need to solve two separate problems. You only combine them if the text says to add them.
asks: Can I add two different groups?
When do I combine two different amounts?
Does the model change if there are two wholes?

facts: Fractions show parts of a whole amount.
The model method helps visualize fraction relationships.
Remainder-of-remainder means subtracting from what is left.
Common denominators are needed for adding or subtracting fractions.

quiz.say: A cake is cut into 8 equal slices. If Liam eats one eighth and Maya eats another eighth, what fraction of the cake is left?
quiz.why: You start with one whole, take away one eighth, and then take away another eighth from the remainder.

wrong.0: This assumes the two parts eaten are equal to half the whole.
wrong.2: This only calculates how much was eaten, not what is left.
wrong.3: This incorrectly adds the two eaten parts together.

quiz.say: A rope is one whole meter long. If you use one third for a gift and one sixth for a project, what fraction of the rope remains?
quiz.why: You must subtract both fractions from one whole, using a common denominator of six.

wrong.1: This only subtracts the first fraction mentioned.
wrong.2: This only considers the second fraction used.
wrong.3: This incorrectly multiplies the two fractions together.

quiz.say: If a box has 10 pencils, and you give away one fifth and then give away another one fifth, how many pencils are left?
quiz.why: First, find one fifth of 10, which is 2. Then, subtract 2 twice from 10.

wrong.0: This treats the second amount as a fraction of the whole, not the remainder.
wrong.2: This only finds the first amount taken away.
wrong.3: This incorrectly adds the two fractions together.
